title: Corpus record
description: One record per candidate paper. corpus.jsonl holds one of these per line.

key.description: Citation key, e.g. sample2025iterative. Must match the key in refs.bib.

id.description: Primary external identifier, e.g. arXiv:2503.01234 or doi:10.1145/…

openalex_id.description: OpenAlex work ID. MUST come from openalex_resolve_name — never guessed. Once set, every further OpenAlex touch of this record is a free singleton lookup.

found_via.description: Which recall mode surfaced this record. If every include has only keyword:* entries, the other three modes contributed nothing and recall is suspect. `watch:<date>` marks records added by a later watch run.

relevance.description: RCS score against the research question, not general quality. Screening is a threshold on this, never a direct judgement.

contextual_summary.description: <=300 words written AGAINST the research question. Not the paper's own abstract.

screen.description: unsure is a first-class terminal state. Forcing a binary call inflates apparent coverage.

axes.description: Values on the taxonomy axes declared in Phase 0. Keys must match coverage.yml axes.

claim.description: One sentence: what this paper actually showed. Open-response, never a checkbox. Required for screen=include.

corroboration.description: Cross-paper agreement on this record's claim, by citation key. Two papers disagreeing is information — never average it away; exits must carry the disagreement, not a smoothed consensus.

agrees_with.description: Keys of corpus records reporting a compatible result.

conflicts_with.description: Keys of corpus records reporting an incompatible result on an overlapping benchmark. Usually they controlled different variables — record which.

numbers.description: Every figure you intend to quote downstream. A number with no source may not appear in any exit.

source.description: Where it lives, e.g. 'Table 3, p.7' or 'Figure 2b'. Finding the right table is harder than reading a given one.

looked_at.description: True only if the table/figure was actually rendered and read, not merely parsed out of text.

evidence_read.description: How deep you actually read. A survey that is 90% abstract-only is a different object from one that is full-text, and nothing else makes that visible.

then.description: An include with no claim is an un-read paper wearing a decision.
